successCriteria.description: EmployeeService class implements IEmployeeService and receives IEmployeeRepository via constructor injection
create(data) constructs an Employee with id from crypto.randomUUID(), employmentStatus=ACTIVE, terminationDate=null, deletedAt=null, createdAt/updatedAt=new Date(), and delegates to repo.create
update(id, data) applies field-level allowlisting — only firstName, lastName, email, managerId, department, hireDate are writable — then delegates to repo.update
terminate(id) fetches the employee first; returns null if not found; otherwise sets employmentStatus=TERMINATED and terminationDate=new Date() then delegates to repo.update
getById, getByEmployeeNumber, getSubordinates delegate directly to the corresponding repository method without transformation

Controller factory makeEmployeeController(service) returns an object with six handler functions: getEmployeeById, getEmployeeByNumber, getSubordinates, createEmployee, updateEmployee, terminateEmployee
Controller handlers return 200 for successful GET/PUT/POST-terminate, 201 for create, and 404 with { error, code } shape when the requested resource is not found
employeeRoutes(fastify, repo) registers six endpoints under /employees prefix: GET /:id, GET /number/:employeeNumber, GET /:managerId/subordinates, POST /, PUT /:id, POST /:id/terminate
Barrel export index.ts re-exports Employee, IEmployeeRepository, CreateEmployeeDto, IEmployeeService, EmployeeService, makeEmployeeController, and employeeRoutes

constraints: All database access must go through IEmployeeRepository — no inline SQL or direct db calls in service, controller, or routes
Service and controller must not import from sibling modules' internals — only from the employee module's own index.ts or shared/types
outOfScope: Unit and integration tests for the employee service — these are produced in Sub-phase 2.3 (Employee service unit tests)

entityInvariants.invariant: A newly created Employee always has employmentStatus=ACTIVE, terminationDate=null, and deletedAt=null — these fields are set by the service, not accepted from the caller's DTO
A terminated Employee must have employmentStatus=TERMINATED and terminationDate set to the time of termination; terminationDate must not be null when status is TERMINATED
Employee id is always a UUID generated via crypto.randomUUID() at creation time — never supplied by the caller

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must return the created Employee; repository failures propagate as-is (no try/catch masking in the service)

Only the allowlisted fields (firstName, lastName, email, managerId, department, hireDate) are forwarded to repo.update; all other keys in the input are silently dropped. Returns null when the employee does not exist.
Returns null when the employee does not exist (idempotent for already-terminated employees — still sets the fields again). Must fetch before mutating to distinguish not-found from update failure.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Employee model must match the canonical fields defined in src/modules/employee/employee.model.ts — id, employeeNumber, firstName, lastName, email, managerId, department, hireDate, terminationDate, employmentStatus, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt
